alerts.headline: Wind Advisory issued September 27 at 5:20AM HST until September 27 at 6:00PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
alerts.description:
* WHAT...East winds 25 to 35 mph with gusts to 55 mph.

* WHERE...Oahu, Kauai, and Niihau. The strongest winds are expected
on Oahu, especially over and downwind of terrain.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM HST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Winds this strong can tear off shingles, knock down tree
branches, blow away tents and awnings and make it difficult to
steer, especially for drivers of high profile vehicles.
alerts.instruction:
Watch out for falling tree branches when walking or driving. Make
sure tents and awnings are secure or take them down. Be prepared for
power outages.

alerts.headline: High Wind Warning issued September 27 at 5:20AM HST until September 27 at 6:00PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
alerts.description:
* WHAT...East winds 30 to 45 mph with gusts up to 75 mph.

* WHERE...Portions of Maui, Big Island, Molokai, and Lanai over and
downwind of terrain, especially in west Maui and Kohala.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM HST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Damaging winds may blow down trees and power lines and
damage roofs. Power outages are possible. Travel will be difficult,
especially for high profile vehicles.
alerts.instruction:
Strong winds may lead to property damage. Hazardous driving
conditions due to powerful cross winds will pose a serious risk for
drivers, especially for light weight and high profile vehicles. Loose
outdoor items should be brought inside or secured properly.

A High Wind Warning means that winds are expected to be at least 40
mph, with gusts over 60 mph. Stay away from downed power lines.

alerts.description:
...HIGH SURF ADVISORY IN EFFECT FOR EAST FACING SHORES OF MOLOKAI,
MAUI, AND THE BIG ISLAND THROUGH THIS EVENING...

...HIGH SURF ADVISORY IN EFFECT FOR SOUTHEAST FACING SHORES OF
THE BIG ISLAND THROUGH THIS EVENING...

...HIGH SURF ADVISORY IN EFFECT FOR EAST FACING SHORES OF KAUAI
AND OAHU THROUGH MONDAY MORNING...

.Southeast swell generated by Hurricane Nolo is beginning to decline
for the Big Island, but continues to produce advisory level surf for
east and southeast facing shores. This swell combined with
gale-force trades is producing advisory level surf along east
facing shores of Maui, Molokai, Oahu and Kauai. Surf will
diminish below advisory criteria later today for the eastern
islands but will likely continue through tonight for Oahu and
Kauai as Nolo moves westward away from the islands.

* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 8 to 12 ft in the morning,
diminishing to 7 to 10 ft by this evening.

* WHERE...East facing shores of Molokai, Maui, and the Big
Island.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM HST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Moderate. Strong breaking waves and strong currents
will make swimming dangerous.

go out.

ACPN50 PHFO 272319
TWOCP 

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 PM HST Sun Sep 27 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Polo, located southwest of Cabo San Lucas, Mexico, on Hurricane
Nolo, located a few hundred miles south-southwest of the Big Island
of Hawaii, on recently upgraded Tropical Storm Rachel, located
several hundred miles southwest of the Acapulco, Mexico, and has
issued the last advisory on Post-Tropical Cyclone Odalys, located
well west of the southern tip of Baja California.

Well East-Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands:
A broad area of low pressure located well east-southeast of the
Hawaiian Islands is producing a large area of showers and
thunderstorms. Recent satellite-derived wind data indicate that the
system is becoming better organized. Environmental conditions are
expected to be conducive for further development, and a tropical
depression is likely to form during the next day or two. The system
should move generally northeastward and remain well east-southeast
of the Hawaiian Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...70 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Storm Rachel are issued under
WMO header WTPZ33 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP3.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Storm Rachel are issued
under WMO header WTPZ23 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP3.

$$
Forecaster Kelly

aiBriefing: Obecnie na Hawajach obowiązują ostrzeżenia przed silnym wiatrem i wysokimi falami, związane głównie z huraganem Nolo przechodzącym blisko wysp — ale wszystkie te alerty wygasają dziś (28 września) lub wygasły już wczoraj wieczorem, czyli zakończą się na długo przed Waszym przylotem 2 października. Poziom zagrożenia 2 ("Podwyższony") odzwierciedla sytuację sprzed startu Waszej podróży, a nie warunki, w jakich będziecie faktycznie podróżować. Ważniejsza jest informacja, że CPHC widzi 90% szans na uformowanie się nowego systemu tropikalnego w ciągu 7 dni, daleko na wschód-południowy wschód od Hawajów — to już mogłoby się rozwijać w czasie Waszej podróży, więc warto śledzić jego rozwój bliżej daty wylotu. Na razie nic nie wskazuje na bezpośrednie zagrożenie dla Oahu, Big Island ani Maui w dniach 2-12 października, ale sytuacja może się zmienić, więc sprawdźcie prognozę ponownie tuż przed wyjazdem.

aiUnnamedSystem.description: Obszar niskiego ciśnienia opisany jako położony daleko na wschód-południowy wschód od Hawajów, poruszający się na północny wschód i pozostający z dala od wysp — brak nazwy i dokładnej pozycji w danych, oszacowanie bardzo przybliżone na podstawie opisu słownego.
